issue_snapshot.title: Can not use `send_denial_response` with `StreamingResponse`
issue_snapshot.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/discussions/2566
Originally posted by **WSH032** April 6, 2024 ## Describe the bug If we use `FileResponse` or `StreamingResponse` when sending the Websocket Denial Response, a `RuntimeError` will occur. ## To Reproduce ```py from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse from uvicorn import run app = FastAPI() @app.websocket("/") async def _(ws: WebSocket): async def foo(): yield "hello" yield "world" resp = StreamingResponse(content=foo()) await ws.send_denial_response(resp) run(app) ``` Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Launch the server 2. Try to establish the websocket connection 3. You will see following error ```console | File "e:\GitHub\fastapi-proxy\Untitled-8.py", line 16, in _ | await ws.send_denial_response(resp) | File "E:\GitHub\fastapi-proxy\.venv\lib\site-packages\starlette\websockets.py", line 209, in send_denial_response | await response(self.scope, self.receive, self.send) | File "E:\GitHub\fastapi-proxy\.venv\lib\site-packages\starlette\responses.py", line 258, in __call__ | async with anyio.create_task_group() as task_group: | File "E:\GitHub\fastapi-proxy\.venv\lib\site-packages\anyio\_backends\_asyncio.py", line 678, in __aexit__ | raise BaseExceptionGroup( | exceptiongroup.ExceptionGroup: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception) +-+---------------- 1 ---------------- | Traceback (most recent call last): | File "E:\GitHub\fastapi-proxy\.venv\lib\site-packages\starlette\responses.py", line 261, in wrap | await func() | File "E:\GitHub\fastapi-proxy\.venv\lib\site-packages\starlette\responses.py", line 243, in stream_response | await send( | File "E:\GitHub\fastapi-proxy\.venv\lib\site-packages\starlette\websockets.py", line 75, in send | raise RuntimeError( | RuntimeError: Expected ASGI message "websocket.accept","websocket.close" or "websocket.http.response.start",but got 'http.response.start' +------------------------------------ ``` ## Expected behavior `FileResponse` and `StreamingResponse` override the `__call__` method, but they do not add the `"websocket."` prefix like the parent class `Response` does. https://github.com/encode/starlette/blob/4e453ce91940cc7c995e6c728e3fdf341c039056/starlette/responses.py#L151-L154 If this is expected behavior, I didn't see any relevant information in the documentation, and at least the type checker didn't raise any errors ## Configuration ``` starlette == 0.37.2 ```

issue_snapshot.title: SessionMiddleware sends a new set-cookie for every request, with unintended results
issue_snapshot.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/encode/starlette/discussions/2018
Originally posted by **sm-Fifteen** January 27, 2023 The way SessionMiddleware currently works is that it encodes session data in a signed base64 object with timestamp, in a format not entirely dissimilar to (but incompatible with) JWT. Because of the way it works, being run right before the headers for an HTTP response are sent, and because it doesn't perform many checks besides whether or not there is session data to encode, it will try to update the session cookie whenever a route is called. This is somewhat wasteful, as session data is not usually updated on every request, but it leads to interesting issues as well. I have a FastAPI application where login is handeled via a session cookie with a separate login process. Several routes are unlocked based on whether or not the cookie is present and based on the user authorizations recorded in said session cookie. When the frontend fetches API data, if the user is logged in, every response contains a new `Set-Cookie` header, which *Firefox ignores, but Chrome acknowledges*. None of the API routes alter session data, so the cookie value is always the same, save for the timestamp and signature at the end. This actually runs into [an interesting Chrome issue](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=696204#c107) where responses to fetch requests that arrive after the page has been navigated away from still alter the session cookie, even if if the new page changed the session data on load. This means I have this strange, Chrome-exclusive, race-condition-y bug that matches lepture/authlib#334, where the session state data setup by the Oauth flow before redirecting to the third party login form may get clobbered if some `/api/slow_route` query was pending when the user clicked the login button. It's unclear if it's actually a chrome bug or unintended behavior from everything working as intended. If Starlette wasn't updating cookies for every request, and the ``Set-Cookie`` was actually important here, it's difficult to argue whether or not Chrome should have ignored it. See here the Starlette test case from the Chromium bug report, which doesn't use SessionMiddleware, but shows the Chrome behavior in action. ```py from starlette.applications import Starlette from starlette.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse, JSONResponse, PlainTextResponse from starlette.routing import Route import uvicorn import datetime from asyncio import sleep html_content = """ Calling slow route via fetch() before changing page. """ async def homepage(request): return HTMLResponse(html_content) async def set_cookie_on_fetch(request): res = JSONResponse({'hello':'world'}) await sleep(5) res.set_cookie("my_cookie", "a__" + datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()) return res async def set_cookie_and_redirect(request): res = RedirectResponse("/final") res.set_cookie("my_cookie", "b__" + datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()) return res async def final(request): cookie_val = request.cookies.get('my_cookie') cookie_is_b = cookie_val.partition("__")[0] == 'b' if (cookie_is_b): res = PlainTextResponse("Cookie value is \"" + cookie_val + "\", all is well. Try refreshing the page.", 200) else: res = PlainTextResponse("Cookie value is \"" + cookie_val + "\", it shouldn't be.", 400) return res routes = [ Route('/', homepage), Route('/set_cookie_on_fetch', set_cookie_on_fetch), Route('/set_cookie_and_redirect', set_cookie_and_redirect), Route('/final', final), ] app = Starlette(debug=True, routes=routes) uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000) ```

issue_snapshot.title: `RuntimeError("No response returned")` in `BaseHTTPMiddleware`
issue_snapshot.body: Previously, a "No response returned"-error has been discussed in this discussion: https://github.com/encode/starlette/discussions/1527, and was supposedly fixed in this PR: https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/1715 However, the bug is still present. It's a race condition, so quite tough to reproduce, but the following reproducer works. Reproducer -- Use anyio 4.2.0 It does happen also with anyio 3.0.0, but it happens much more regularly on 4.2. First, apply the following patch to the Starlette codebase, so that we have a breakpoint in case it happens: ```diff --- a/starlette/middleware/base.py +++ b/starlette/middleware/base.py @@ -134,7 +134,8 @@ class BaseHTTPMiddleware: async def send_no_error(message: Message) -> None: try: @@ -163,6 +164,7 @@ class BaseHTTPMiddleware: except anyio.EndOfStream: if app_exc is not None: raise app_exc + breakpoint() raise RuntimeError("No response returned.") assert message["type"] == "http.response.start" ``` Then run this code: ```python import asyncio from hypercorn.asyncio import serve from hypercorn.config import Config from starlette.applications import Starlette from starlette.responses import JSONResponse from starlette.routing import Route from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware from starlette.requests import Request from starlette.responses import Response from starlette.middleware.base import RequestResponseEndpoint from starlette.middleware import Middleware class DummyMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware): async def dispatch( self, request: Request, call_next: RequestResponseEndpoint ) -> Response: return await call_next(request) async def homepage(request): return JSONResponse({}) app = Starlette( routes=[ Route("/", homepage), ], middleware=[Middleware(DummyMiddleware) for i in range(100)], # Yes, 100x the same middleware. ) config = Config.from_mapping({}) config.bind = ["127.0.0.1:8000"] asyncio.run(serve(app, config)) ``` Open either Firefox or Chrome, navigate to http://localhost:8000 and hold down command-r (refresh) to repeatedly have the browser refresh the page. After a couple of seconds, we'll enter the breakpoint. (Feel free to turn this issue into a discussion if that's more appropriate. I'm also looking for a fix but have a hard time understanding `BaseHTTPMiddleware`.) edit: I updated the above snippet and added the missing imports. This PR contains a possible fix: https://github.com/encode/starlette/pull/2519 > [!IMPORTANT] > - We're using [Polar.sh](https://polar.sh/encode) so you can upvote and help fund this issue. > - We receive the funding once the issue is completed & confirmed by you. > - Thank you in advance for helping prioritize & fund our backlog.

issue_snapshot.title: Request Header cookie parsing doesn't follow RFC 7540 spec
issue_snapshot.body:
Only the first cookie in a header gets parsed. but multiple "cookie" headers may be sent and the server should concatenate them per [RFC 7540](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7540)

```
...
   If there are multiple Cookie header fields after
   decompression, these MUST be concatenated into a single octet string
   using the two-octet delimiter of 0x3B, 0x20 (the ASCII string "; ")
   before being passed into a non-HTTP/2 context, such as an HTTP/1.1
   connection, or a generic HTTP server application.

   Therefore, the following two lists of Cookie header fields are
   semantically equivalent.

     cookie: a=b; c=d; e=f

     cookie: a=b
     cookie: c=d
     cookie: e=f
```

The issue lies here
https://github.com/encode/starlette/blob/6ee94f2cac955eeae68d2898a8dec8cf17b48736/starlette/requests.py#L143

---

Originally posted by **wpk-nist-gov** May 26, 2026 ### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorials in the docs and didn't find an answer. ### Example Code ```python from typing import Annotated import typer app = typer.Typer() @app.command("arg") def from_argument(user: Annotated[str, typer.Argument(envvar="ME")]): print(f"Hello {user}") @app.command("opt") def from_option(user: Annotated[str, typer.Option(envvar="ME")]): print(f"Hello {user}") if __name__ == "__main__": app() ``` ### Description The `envvar` option is not respected for `typer.Option`. issue_snapshot.body:
This might seem like a contrived example, but it honestly happened my first time trying out the new auto-scrolling on select feature.

I ran the textual demo and started trying to select the text on the home page. The notification toast ends up getting selected as well, which actually prevents the auto-scrolling.

After the waiting for the notification to timeout and moving the mouse to try to auto-scroll the selection, the app crashes with `ValueError: No common ancestor found`.

Perhaps the notifications just shouldn't be included in the selection, but presumably this could be a problem with any widget that could be removed from the DOM?

issue_snapshot.title: Height not refreshed after remove_childre
issue_snapshot.body:
Have you checked closed issues? Yes

Have you checked against the most recent version of Textual? Yes

## The bug

Here as an example to reproduce.

```python
from textual.app import App, ComposeResult
from textual.containers import VerticalGroup
from textual.widgets import Static
from textual.binding import Binding


class ExampleApp(App):
    BINDINGS = [Binding("c", "clear", priority=True)]

    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
        yield Static("Hello")
        with VerticalGroup():
            for i in range(10):
                yield Static(str(i))
        yield Static("World")

    async def action_clear(self) -> None:
        vs = self.query_one(VerticalGroup)
        await vs.remove_children()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = ExampleApp()
    app.run()
```

After pressing "c" the children of VerticalGroup are removed but it is not being shrunk. The issue seems to first appear in textual==6.3.0

issue_snapshot.title: _run_vars memory leak
issue_snapshot.body:
### Things to check first

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and didn't find my bug already reported there

- [x] I have checked that my bug is still present in the latest release


### AnyIO version

85b8b6e, a few commits past 4.14.1 tag

### Python version

3.12

### What happened?

I noticed memory continually climbing during a loop that invokes to_thread.run_sync until OOM killed it.

The rest of this bug report is from Fable

## `_run_vars` leaks every `anyio.run()`'s event loop, root task, and result

Each call to `anyio.run()` that uses `anyio.to_thread.run_sync()` (asyncio
backend) permanently leaks the event loop, the root task, and the root
task's result (the return value of the coroutine passed to `anyio.run()`).
Calling `anyio.run()` in a loop with large results grows memory without
bound; `gc.collect()` does not reclaim it.

Tested against git `master` (`85b8b6e`, 10 commits past the `4.14.1` tag),
Python 3.12.3, Linux x86_64. Confirmed on the asyncio backend; the trio
backend does not leak (`run_sync_in_worker_thread` on trio doesn't go
through `find_root_task`/`_root_task`, so nothing gets cached in
`_run_vars`).

### Cause

`find_root_task()` in `anyio/_backends/_asyncio.py` caches the root task via
`_root_task.set(task)`, into the per-loop dict in `anyio/lowlevel.py`'s
`_run_vars` `WeakKeyDictionary` (keyed by the loop). That cached `Task`
object keeps the loop and the task's result alive, so the entry's value
holds a strong reference back to its own weak key — the dict never evicts
it, and nothing ever pops it on run teardown.

### Suggested fix

Pop the run's `_run_vars` entry when the run finishes, e.g.
`_run_vars.pop(token, None)` in a `finally` around `asyncio.run()`'s runner
in `anyio/_backends/_asyncio.py`. Note this applies to any RunVar value
that transitively references a task or the loop, not just `_root_task`.

### Workaround

Between `anyio.run()` calls (when no loop is running):

```python
import anyio.lowlevel
anyio.lowlevel._run_vars.clear()
```


### How can we reproduce the bug?


```python
import gc, os
import anyio, anyio.lowlevel, anyio.to_thread

def rss_mb():
    with open("/proc/self/statm") as f:
        return int(f.read().split()[1]) * os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") / 1024 / 1024

def work() -> bytes:
    return b"x" * 50_000_000

async def main() -> bytes:
    return await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(work)

for i in range(10):
    data = anyio.run(main)
    del data
    gc.collect()
    print(f"[{i}] RSS {rss_mb():6.0f} MB  _run_vars entries={len(anyio.lowlevel._run_vars)}")
```

Output:

```
[0] RSS     71 MB  _run_vars entries=1
[1] RSS    119 MB  _run_vars entries=2
[2] RSS    166 MB  _run_vars entries=3
...
[9] RSS    500 MB  _run_vars entries=10
```

### Things to check first

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and didn't find my bug already reported there

- [x] I have checked that my bug is still present in the latest release


### AnyIO version

master (2ba69a649011e4608ab9485a0dcfe72b6f956ecc)

### Python version

CPython 3.13.14

### What happened?

For `TaskGroup.start` tasks on Trio, the default ``TaskHandle.name`` does not match the task name (`TaskInfo.name`). It's missing the module name.

### How can we reproduce the bug?

All three of these assertions fail on Trio:

```python
async def test_start_name_default() -> None:
    """
    This is similar to ``TestCreateTask.test_task_name_default``, but for ``start``
    instead of ``create_task``.
    """

    async def taskfunc(*, task_status: TaskStatus[None]) -> str | None:
        task_status.started()
        return get_current_task().name

    async with create_task_group() as tg:
        handle = await tg.start(taskfunc, return_handle=True)
        assert re.match(
            r"<TaskHandle finished name='tests.test_taskgroups.test_start_name_default.<locals>.taskfunc' "
            r"coro=<coroutine object test_start_name_default.<locals>.taskfunc at 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+>>",
            repr(handle),
        )
        assert await handle == handle.name

    assert (
        handle.name == "tests.test_taskgroups.test_start_name_default.<locals>.taskfunc"
    )
```

DependedValue: TypeAlias = Annotated[int, Depends(some_value)] # This won't work. # type DependedValue = Annotated[int, Depends(some_value)] @app.get('/') async def get_with_dep(value: DependedValue) -> str: print(f'{type(value) = !r}') print(f'{value = !r}') assert isinstance(value, int), '`value` should be an integer.' assert value == 123, '`value` should be 123.' return f'value: {value}' ``` ### Description When using the method in line 15: ```python DependedValue: TypeAlias = Annotated[int, Depends(some_value)] ``` to declare a type alias, FastAPI correctly interprets it and fills the `value` with `123` for `get_with_dep`. issue_snapshot.title: SSE `stream_item_type` not propagated through `APIRouter` + `include_router`
issue_snapshot.body:
### Summary

When an SSE route (`response_class=EventSourceResponse` + `AsyncIterator[Frame]` return annotation) is defined on an `APIRouter` and then merged onto a `FastAPI` app via `include_router`, the resulting merged route loses its `stream_item_type`. As a consequence, the OpenAPI `text/event-stream` response schema omits the `data.contentSchema`, so tooling like `datamodel-codegen` cannot generate frame models.

Defining the same route directly on the `FastAPI` app via `@app.post(...)` works correctly.

### Reproduction

```python
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from fastapi.sse import EventSourceResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel


class Frame(BaseModel):
    kind: str


# Case A — route registered directly on the app: works
app_a = FastAPI()

@app_a.post("/s", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
async def a() -> AsyncIterator[Frame]:
    yield Frame(kind="x")


# Case B — route defined on a router, then `include_router`: broken
router = APIRouter()

@router.post("/s", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
async def b() -> AsyncIterator[Frame]:
    yield Frame(kind="x")


app_b = FastAPI()
app_b.include_router(router)

print("DIRECT:", app_a.routes[-1].stream_item_type)
print("ROUTER (pre-include):", router.routes[-1].stream_item_type)
print("APP (post-include):", app_b.routes[-1].stream_item_type)


def has_content_schema(spec: dict) -> bool:
    sse = spec["paths"]["/s"]["post"]["responses"]["200"]["content"]["text/event-stream"]
    return "contentSchema" in sse.get("itemSchema", {}).get("properties", {}).get("data", {})


print("DIRECT openapi has contentSchema:", has_content_schema(app_a.openapi()))
print("INCLUDE_ROUTER openapi has contentSchema:", has_content_schema(app_b.openapi()))
```

Output:

```
DIRECT: <class '__main__.Frame'>
ROUTER (pre-include): <class '__main__.Frame'>
APP (post-include): None

DIRECT openapi has contentSchema: True
INCLUDE_ROUTER openapi has contentSchema: False
```

### Expected

After `include_router`, the merged route on `app_b` should carry the same `stream_item_type` as the source route, and the emitted OpenAPI should include the `contentSchema` under `responses.200.content["text/event-stream"].itemSchema.properties.data` referencing `Frame`.

### Actual

The merged route's `stream_item_type` is `None`; the emitted OpenAPI shows the generic SSE envelope (`data: string, event, id, retry`) with no `contentSchema`.

### Root cause (proposed)

In `fastapi/routing.py`, `APIRoute.__init__` populates `self.stream_item_type` only inside the branch guarded by `isinstance(response_model, DefaultPlaceholder)`:

```python
if isinstance(response_model, DefaultPlaceholder):
    return_annotation = get_typed_return_annotation(endpoint)
    if lenient_issubclass(return_annotation, Response):
        response_model = None
    else:
        stream_item = get_stream_item_type(return_annotation)
        if stream_item is not None:
            if (
                isinstance(response_class, DefaultPlaceholder)
                or lenient_issubclass(response_class, EventSourceResponse)
            ) and not lenient_issubclass(stream_item, ServerSentEvent):
                self.stream_item_type = stream_item
            response_model = None
        else:
            response_model = return_annotation
self.response_model = response_model
```

When the source route (on the `APIRouter`) is created, `response_model` starts as a `DefaultPlaceholder`, the detection runs, and `self.response_model` is overwritten to `None`.

`APIRouter.include_router` then creates the merged route with:

```python
self.add_api_route(
    prefix + route.path,
    route.endpoint,
    response_model=route.response_model,  # now None, not DefaultPlaceholder
    ...
    response_class=use_response_class,
    ...
)
```

On the merged route's `__init__`, `isinstance(response_model, DefaultPlaceholder)` is now `False`, so the detection branch is skipped and `self.stream_item_type` stays at its initial `None`.

The symmetric issue likely affects JSONL streaming (`response_class=DefaultPlaceholder` path) too, since it's gated by the same `DefaultPlaceholder` check on `response_model`.

### Suggested fix

Either:
1. In `include_router`, additionally copy `stream_item_type` onto the new route (simplest, closest to the current wiring).
2. In `APIRoute.__init__`, run stream-item detection regardless of whether `response_model` is a `DefaultPlaceholder`, as long as `response_model is None` after the conditional.

### Environment

- `fastapi==0.135.2`
- `pydantic==2.12.5`
- `starlette==1.0.0`
- Python `3.11.6`
- macOS 14.4.1

Happy to open a PR if the preferred fix direction is specified.

    test_with =  getattr(metafunc.function, 'test_with', None)

issue_snapshot.title: Variables injected in doctest_namespace no longer loaded in Pytest 9.1.x
issue_snapshot.body:
### Description

I'm running into issues with `pytest` 9.1.x when running my doctests. I've been able to inject variables and functions into the namespace for doctests via a fixture so that I don't need to explicitly write these things into all my doctests, e.g.:
```python
@pytest.fixture(scope="session", autouse=True)
def doctest_setup(doctest_namespace, nimbus, worker_id, open_dataset) -> None:  # numpydoc ignore=PR01
    """Gather testing data on doctest run."""
    testing_setup_warnings()
    gather_testing_data(worker_cache_dir=nimbus.path, worker_id=worker_id)
    doctest_namespace.update(custom_testing_data(nimbus=nimbus))

    class AttrDict(dict):  # numpydoc ignore=PR01
        """A dictionary that allows access to its keys as attributes."""

        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
            self.__dict__ = self

    xr = AttrDict()
    xr["DataArray"] = xarray.DataArray
    xr["date_range"] = xarray.date_range
    xr["open_dataset"] = custom_library.open_dataset
    doctest_namespace["xr"] = xr

    doctest_namespace.update(add_doctest_filepaths())
    doctest_namespace.update(add_example_file_paths())
```

This has been working well for many years, but it seems like there's been a major change in how the latest `pytest` collects/runs fixtures for doctests.

All my tests are now failing with `NameError: name '<variable/function name injected from doctest_setup>' is not defined`.

issue_snapshot.title: help not resolving automatically
issue_snapshot.body:
From the docs: 

The help parameter is implemented in Click in a very special manner. Unlike regular parameters it’s automatically added by Click for any command and it performs automatic conflict resolution. By default it’s called --help, but this can be changed. If a command itself implements a parameter with the same name, the default help parameter stops accepting it. There is a context setting that can be used to override the names of the help parameters called [help_option_names](https://click.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/api/#click.Context.help_option_names).

What is wrong: 
Help does not automatically resolve if there is an arg or kwarg called help. In the sample the file is called help.py

``` 
import click

# This works 
@click.command()
@click.argument('helps')
def this_works(helps):
    print(helps)

# > python -m help this
# this

# > python -m help --help
# Usage: help.py [OPTIONS] HELPS

# Options:
#   --help  Show this message and exit.

# This does not work
@click.command()
@click.argument('help')
def this_does_not_work(help):
    print(help)

# > python -m help this
# Usage: help.py [OPTIONS] HELP
# Try 'help.py --help' for help.

# Error: Invalid value for '--help': 'this' is not a valid boolean.

# > python -m help --help
# Usage: help.py [OPTIONS] HELP
# Try 'help.py --help' for help.

# Error: Missing argument 'HELP'.

# This does not work
@click.command()
@click.option('--help', default='this_2')
def this_does_not_work_also(help='this_2'):
    print(help)

# > python -m help 
# None

# > python -m help --help
# Error: Option '--help' requires an argument.

if __name__ == '__main__':
    #this_works()
    #this_does_not_work()
    this_does_not_work_also()

```
- Python version: 3.10.15
- Click version: 8.1.7

issue_snapshot.title: `TypeAdapter` with Union has `Any` type hint argument starting with Pydantic 2.7.0+
issue_snapshot.body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Hi, with Pydantic versions 2.7.0+, I cannot have proper type hints for `TypeAdapter` in combination with `Union` / `|`. Versions 2.6.x work properly (see example below). Note this is about type hints for the IDE and not about runtime validation. Most recent Pyright/Basedpyright `v1.12.4 (pyright 1.1.365)` is used as Language server, but issue is independent of its used version.

### Pydantic v2.6.4
(Comments show static type hints by IDE)
```python
from pydantic import TypeAdapter

ad1 = TypeAdapter(str | int) # ad1: TypeAdapter[UnionType]
ad2 = TypeAdapter[str | int](str | int) # ad1: TypeAdapter[str | int]

result1 = ad1.validate_python("foo") # result1: UnionType
result2 = ad2.validate_python(42) # result2: str | int

If no manual type is given, type argument is `UnionType`.

### Pydantic v2.7.0+
(Comments show static type hints by IDE)

result2 = ad2.validate_python(42) # result2: Any

issue_snapshot.title: Generic __pydantic_extra__ typevar substitution lost in non-generic subclasses of parametrized models
issue_snapshot.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2 (`main` @ 428b0dba8)
- [x] I have searched GitHub for a duplicate issue and I'm sure this is something new

### Description

Follow-up to #13369 / #13391 (`__pydantic_extra__` typevar substitution, currently main-only): the substitution works for direct parametrization (`M[int]`) but is lost in a plain (non-generic) subclass of a parametrized model (`class Sub(M[int])`). Extras on the subclass are silently **unvalidated** and the JSON schema loses the extras type.

```
M[int](x='nope')  -> ValidationError (correct, fixed by #13391)
Sub(x='nope')     -> accepted; m.x == 'nope'          # BUG
Sub(x='5').x      -> '5' (str)  vs  M[int](x='5').x == 5

M[int].model_json_schema()['additionalProperties']  -> {'type': 'integer'}
Sub.model_json_schema()['additionalProperties']     -> {}                  # BUG
Sub.__pydantic_extra_info__                          -> PydanticExtraInfo(annotation=dict[str, ~T], complete=True)
```

Root cause (from stepping through `collect_model_fields` in `pydantic/_internal/_fields.py`): for `Sub`, `typevars_map` is empty (its own `__pydantic_generic_metadata__` is empty) and the inherited hint for `__pydantic_extra__` is the parent's *raw* annotation `dict[str, T]` — so `_generics.replace_types(ann, typevars_map)` is a no-op and the raw `~T` survives, producing `extras_schema = {'type': 'any'}`. Regular fields don't have this problem because they're copied from the parent's already-substituted `model_fields`; the extra-info path never consults the parent's `__pydantic_extra_info__` (which on `M[int]` correctly holds `dict[str, int]`).

Note the 2-level generic chain (`class Mid(M[T], Generic[T])`; `Mid[int]`) works on main — only the plain-subclass case is broken.

I have a small fix working locally (reuse the parent's substituted `PydanticExtraInfo` annotation when `__pydantic_extra__` is only inherited, mirroring how fields inherit; brings extra-info to exact parity with fields, including the same known deferred-annotation limitation as #12000), with a regression test in the style of `test_extra_generic_class` — it passes the `test_main.py` / `test_generics.py` / `test_forward_ref.py` / `test_edge_cases.py` suites with no new failures. Per the contributing guidelines I'd like to be assigned before opening the PR — happy to submit it right away.

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Generic, TypeVar
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

T = TypeVar('T')

class M(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')
    __pydantic_extra__: dict[str, T]
    y: T

class Sub(M[int]):
    pass

print(Sub(y=1, x='not_an_int').x)  # 'not_an_int' — should raise ValidationError
print(Sub.model_json_schema().get('additionalProperties'))  # {} — should be {'type': 'integer'}
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```text
pydantic version: 2.14.0a1
pydantic-core version: 2.47.0
python version: 3.14.4
platform: macOS-26.5-arm64
commit: 428b0dba8 (main)
```

issue_snapshot.title: Experimental pipeline: every constraint chained after `ge`/`lt`/`le` is dropped from the JSON schema
issue_snapshot.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

In the experimental pipeline API, chaining constraints silently drops every bound after the first from the generated JSON schema. **Validation stays correct** - only the published schema is wrong, which makes it easy to miss.

All bounds below are non-zero, so this is not #13450 (falsy zero bounds in `Interval`). Observed identically on released 2.13.4 and on `main` (2.14.0a1).

| expression | JSON schema | validation |
|---|---|---|
| `validate_as(int).ge(1).le(100)` | `{"minimum": 1, "type": "integer"}` | 0 reject, 50 accept, 200 reject |
| `validate_as(int).le(100).ge(1)` | `{"maximum": 100, "type": "integer"}` | 0 reject, 50 accept, 200 reject |
| `validate_as(int).constrain(Interval(ge=1, le=100))` | `{"minimum": 1, "type": "integer"}` | 0 reject, 50 accept, 200 reject |
| `validate_as(int).ge(1).le(100).multiple_of(5)` | `{"minimum": 1, "type": "integer"}` | correct |
| `validate_as(int).gt(1).lt(100)` *(control)* | `{"exclusiveMinimum": 1, "exclusiveMaximum": 100, ...}` | correct |
| `Annotated[int, Ge(1), Le(100)]` *(control)* | `{"minimum": 1, "maximum": 100, ...}` | correct |

So `.ge(1).le(100).multiple_of(5)` publishes a schema advertising *any integer >= 1*, while the validator rejects 200 and 52. For FastAPI that means the OpenAPI component and every generated client disagree with the server.

### Cause

In `_apply_constraint()`, the `Ge`, `Lt` and `Le` branches apply their fallback function validator **unconditionally** - including when the native core-schema field was just set:

```python
elif isinstance(constraint, annotated_types.Ge):
    ge = constraint.ge
    if s and s['type'] in {'int', 'float', 'decimal'}:
        s = s.copy()
        if s['type'] == 'int' and isinstance(ge, int):
            s['ge'] = ge          # native constraint applied...
        ...

    def check_ge(v: Any) -> bool:
        return v >= ge

    s = _check_func(check_ge, f'>= {ge}', s)   # ...and then wrapped anyway
```

`_check_func` wraps the schema in `function-after`. The next constraint in the chain sees `s['type'] == 'function-after'`, which is not in `{'int', 'float', 'decimal'}`, so it cannot set its own native field and survives only inside an opaque callable that JSON-schema generation cannot read. Core schema for `.ge(1).le(100)`:

```
{'type': 'function-after',
 'function': ...,                       # <- le(100) lives in here, invisible to the schema
 'schema': {'type': 'function-after',
            'function': ...,            # <- redundant ge check
            'schema': {'type': 'int', 'ge': 1}}}
```

`Gt` is the control that works, and only by accident: its fallback sits in an `else:`, so nothing is wrapped when the native constraint applies.

### Relationship to the open PRs in this function

Two in-flight PRs each fix one branch of this, for unrelated reasons, and between them they leave `Ge`, `Lt` and `Le` untouched:

- **#13473** adds a `native_constraint_applied` flag to `MultipleOf` to avoid a float parity problem. Same shape as the fix needed here.
- **#13446** restructures `Gt` so the fallback lands inside the numeric branch.

Worth flagging on the second one: #13446's description argues that `Gt` is *uniquely* broken and holds up `Ge`/`Lt`/`Le`/`MultipleOf` as the correct model, because they "always apply" the check and so enforce the bound on a type mismatch. That is true of validation, but always applying it is exactly what destroys the schema. `Gt` is uniquely broken for validation; the other four are broken for schema. Whichever way this is fixed, it probably wants to be one symmetric change across all five branches rather than three separate patches.

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from pydantic.experimental.pipeline import validate_as

ta = TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, validate_as(int).ge(1).le(100)])

print(ta.json_schema())      # {'minimum': 1, 'type': 'integer'}   <- no maximum
ta.validate_python(200)      # ValidationError, as it should be

# control: the same constraints without the pipeline
import annotated_types
print(TypeAdapter(Annotated[int, annotated_types.Ge(1), annotated_types.Le(100)]).json_schema())
# {'maximum': 100, 'minimum': 1, 'type': 'integer'}
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```text
             pydantic version: 2.13.4
        pydantic-core version: 2.46.4
          pydantic-core build: profile=release pgo=false
               python version: 3.11.15 (main, Mar  3 2026, 09:26:23) [GCC 13.3.0]
                     platform: Linux-6.18.5-x86_64-with-glibc2.39
             related packages: typing_extensions-4.16.0
                       commit: unknown
```

I have a PR ready that applies the `native_constraint_applied` shape from #13473 to `Ge`/`Lt`/`Le`, with regression tests that fail without it. Happy to open it, or to fold it into one of the existing PRs if you'd rather land a single change.

issue_snapshot.title: Generic model parametrization drops field defaults and typevar substitution after `__annotations__` is read on a metaclass (Python <= 3.13)
issue_snapshot.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

This is a regression on `main` (`2.14.0a1`); I could not reproduce it on any released version (checked 2.13.4 and 2.10.6 under the same conditions). It affects Python 3.10–3.13 (verified on 3.10, 3.12 and 3.13); Python 3.14 is unaffected.

If `__annotations__` has ever been **read** on a metaclass appearing in a model's metatype MRO (e.g. `ModelMetaclass` itself, or `abc.ABCMeta`), then any generic model parametrized **for the first time afterwards** gets a broken schema:

- type variables are not substituted (`x: T` ends up with an `any` schema), and
- field defaults are dropped (fields with defaults become required).

Parametrizations built *before* the read keep working, since their schemas are already cached — which makes this very order-dependent and confusing to track down in a real test suite.

Reading an attribute sounds like an odd trigger, but it happens in the wild: on CPython ≤ 3.13, reading `__annotations__` on a (heap) class that has none **auto-creates a plain `__annotations__ = {}` entry in that class's `__dict__`** (see the [annotations HOWTO](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/annotations.html)). `langgraph` does such a read at import time (`get_cached_annotated_keys` in `langgraph/_internal/_fields.py` has a `getattr(base, "__annotations__", None)` fallback — added for Python 3.14 compat, ironically — which ends up planting `{}` on `abc.ABCMeta`). So a plain `import langgraph.prebuilt` breaks all subsequently-parametrized generic models. We found this via the `pydantic/logfire` weekly CI job testing against pydantic main, where `pydantic_evals.Dataset.from_dict()` fails with `3 validation errors for _DatasetModel[...]` — `Field required` for exactly its three defaulted fields — but only in test runs where a langchain test ran first ([failing run](https://github.com/pydantic/logfire/actions/runs/30268424934)).

**Mechanism:**

1. The planted `{}` lives in the metaclass's `__dict__`. For a model class `M`, attribute lookup of `M.__annotations__` searches `type(M).__mro__` (e.g. `(ModelMetaclass, ABCMeta, type, object)`) and now finds the plain dict **before** reaching the `type.__annotations__` getset descriptor. A plain dict is not a data descriptor, so lookup falls back to `M`'s own MRO — and for a class with no own `__annotations__` (like a freshly created generic submodel), this returns **the parent's annotations**. (Normally the `type.__annotations__` data descriptor intercepts the lookup and auto-creates/returns the class's own empty dict, which is what makes `getattr` look safe.)
2. `safe_get_annotations()` in `pydantic/_internal/_typing_extra.py` uses `getattr(obj, '__annotations__', {})` on < 3.14, so for the new submodel `G[str]` it returns the origin's annotations instead of `{}`:
   ```
   clean:    safe_get_annotations(G[str]) == {}
   poisoned: safe_get_annotations(G[str]) == {'x': ~T, 'a': <class 'int'>}
   ```
3. In `collect_model_fields()`, `cls_annotations` is "only used to determine if an annotation comes from a parent class". The leak makes `ann_name in cls_annotations` true for every inherited field, so instead of copying the parent `FieldInfo` and applying `typevars_map` (via `_recreate_field_info`), it takes the plain `FieldInfo.from_annotation(ann_type)` branch: no typevar substitution, and no default — the origin's class-attribute default is long gone because it was `delattr`'d during the origin's own field collection.

**Possible fix:** for classes on ≤ 3.13, read own annotations via `obj.__dict__.get('__annotations__', {})` (what `inspect.get_annotations()` does) rather than `getattr`. Both call sites of `safe_get_annotations()` seem to want own-class annotations anyway: `get_model_type_hints()` iterates the MRO itself and calls it per base, and `cls_annotations` in `collect_model_fields()` is explicitly meant to be the current class's own annotations.

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Generic, TypeVar

from pydantic import BaseModel

# The trigger: any read of `__annotations__` on a metaclass. On CPython <= 3.13 this
# auto-creates a plain `__annotations__ = {}` entry in the metaclass's `__dict__`,
# which shadows the `type.__annotations__` data descriptor for every model class.
# `abc.ABCMeta.__annotations__` has the same effect, and `import langgraph.prebuilt`
# performs an equivalent read at import time.
type(BaseModel).__annotations__

T = TypeVar('T')


class G(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    x: T
    a: int = 5


G[str].model_validate({'x': 'hi'})
```

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for G[str]
a
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'x': 'hi'}, input_type=dict]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.14/v/missing
```

Removing the `type(BaseModel).__annotations__` line — or moving the `G[str]` parametrization above it — makes it pass. To run against main:

```bash
uv run --isolated --no-project --python 3.13 --with "pydantic @ git+https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic.git" repro.py
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```text
             pydantic version: 2.14.0a1
        pydantic-core version: 2.47.0
          pydantic-core build: profile=release pgo=false
               python version: 3.13.0 (main, Oct 12 2024, 20:24:27) [Clang 15.0.0 (clang-1500.3.9.4)]
                     platform: macOS-26.5.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
             related packages: mypy-2.3.0 pyright-1.1.411 email-validator-2.3.0 fastapi-0.139.2 pydantic-settings-2.14.2 typing_extensions-4.16.0
                       commit: a187a65467a588ccc00761d80f325b45381ca819
```

issue_snapshot.title: Different rounding for timestamp and datetime when set last_modified
issue_snapshot.body:
Setting the `last_modified` property of `StreamResponse` rounds the value to seconds if it is `float` or `datetime`. But different rounding mode is used for `float` or `datetime`. If it is a `float` (timestamp), it is rounded toward +infinity. If it is an instance of `datetime`, it is rounded toward -infinity.

For example:
```
$ cat test_last_modified.py
from aiohttp.web import StreamResponse
from datetime import datetime, timezone

resp = StreamResponse()
dt = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
resp.last_modified = dt
print(resp.last_modified)
print(repr(resp.last_modified))
print(resp.headers["Last-Modified"])
resp.last_modified = dt.timestamp()
print(resp.last_modified)
print(repr(resp.last_modified))
print(resp.headers["Last-Modified"])
```
```
$ python test_last_modified.py
2020-12-02 09:51:02+00:00
datetime.datetime(2020, 12, 2, 9, 51, 2, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
Wed, 02 Dec 2020 09:51:02 GMT
2020-12-02 09:51:03+00:00
datetime.datetime(2020, 12, 2, 9, 51, 3, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
Wed, 02 Dec 2020 09:51:03 GMT
```
I don't know what direction is correct, but it should be the same.

issue_snapshot.title: BaseRequest.text() leaks UnicodeDecodeError for bodies that fail to decode with the declared charset
issue_snapshot.body:
### Describe the bug

`BaseRequest.text()` and the `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` branch of `BaseRequest.post()` catch `LookupError` (an invalid charset name) and re-raise as `HTTPUnsupportedMediaType` (415), but they do not catch `UnicodeDecodeError` (the body bytes are not valid for the declared charset). The result is a raw `UnicodeDecodeError` reaching the user, with a frame pointing at `bytes_body.decode(encoding)` instead of a clean 415.

`text()` is the public name users reach for when they want the body as a string, and the existing test `test_request_with_wrong_content_type_encoding` already asserts that the wrong-charset-name case maps to 415 — the wrong-bytes case should behave the same.

### To Reproduce

```python
import asyncio
from aiohttp.test_utils import make_mocked_request
from aiohttp import web

async def main():
    from aiohttp.base_protocol import BaseProtocol
    from aiohttp.streams import StreamReader
    from aiohttp.helpers import DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE

    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    protocol = BaseProtocol(loop=loop)
    payload = StreamReader(protocol, DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE, loop=loop)
    payload.feed_data(b"\xff\xfe")
    payload.feed_eof()
    req = make_mocked_request("POST", "/", payload=payload, headers={"Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"})
    print(await req.text())  # UnicodeDecodeError leaks

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Expected behavior

The decode error should map to `HTTPUnsupportedMediaType` (415), matching the existing behaviour for an invalid charset name. The `text()` docstring already says "Return BODY as text using encoding from .charset" — the implicit promise is that charset/bytes mismatches surface as 415, not as a leaked decode exception.

### Logs/tracebacks

```python-traceback
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/user/repro.py", line 17, in <module>
    asyncio.run(main())
  ...
  File "/path/to/aiohttp/web_request.py", line 644, in text
    return bytes_body.decode(encoding)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte
```

### Notes

The same problem exists in the urlencoded branch of `post()` (line 769 of `web_request.py`): `bytes_query.decode(charset)` is also wrapped in `except LookupError`, so the same body that triggers a leaked exception from `text()` will also leak from `post()` if the request Content-Type is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

issue_snapshot.title: Handle `NotImplementedError: unsupported platform` case.
issue_snapshot.body:
If these three things occur...

* The user is using httpcore either with standard sync, or with `asyncio`.
* The `trio` package happens to be installed.
* We are running on a platform that's unsupported by Trio.

Then there's a case where an import of `trio` can occur and trigger a `NotImplementedError: unsupported platform` exception. (https://github.com/python-trio/trio/issues/3013)

I'd suggest:

* We start with a nice simple fix, and catch the case here... https://github.com/encode/httpcore/blob/ba3f94268e9843b1f60bd4699c15b05a9af7a929/httpcore/_synchronization.py#L12
* Ideally we ensure that we don't run `import trio` or `import anyio` unless we're actually running async.

issue_snapshot.title: WSGIRequestHandler sends 100 Continue twice when client sends Expect: 100-continue
issue_snapshot.body:
`WSGIRequestHandler` sends `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` twice when a client includes the `Expect: 100-continue` header. Python's `BaseHTTPRequestHandler.parse_request()` calls `handle_expect_100()` which sends the first response. Then `run_wsgi()` ([serving.py L313-314](https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/blob/main/src/werkzeug/serving.py#L313-L314)) independently checks the same header and writes a second one. Neither layer clears the header after acting on it.

HTTP clients that strictly parse interim responses — notably the AWS SDK's Netty-based async client — treat the second `100 Continue` as the start of the final response, causing all uploads to fail with status code 100.

```python
import socket
import threading
from werkzeug.serving import make_server


def app(environ, start_response):
    # Read and discard request body
    environ["wsgi.input"].read()
    start_response("200 OK", [("Content-Type", "text/plain")])
    return [b"ok"]


server = make_server("127.0.0.1", 9876, app, threaded=True)
thread = threading.Thread(target=server.handle_request)
thread.start()

sock = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 9876))
sock.sendall(
    b"PUT /test HTTP/1.1\r\n"
    b"Host: 127.0.0.1:9876\r\n"
    b"Content-Length: 5\r\n"
    b"Expect: 100-continue\r\n"
    b"\r\n"
)

# Collect the full response before sending the body
import time
time.sleep(0.5)
response = sock.recv(4096)
print(response.decode())

sock.sendall(b"hello")
time.sleep(0.5)
response = sock.recv(4096)
print(response.decode())

sock.close()
thread.join()
server.server_close()

```

**Expected:** One `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` response, followed by the final `200 OK` after the body is sent.

**Actual:** Two `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` responses are sent before the final `200 OK`. Raw output:

```
HTTP/1.1 100 Continue

HTTP/1.1 100 Continue

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
...
```

A minimal fix would be to override `handle_expect_100` to suppress the stdlib's response, since `run_wsgi()` already handles it:

```python
def handle_expect_100(self) -> bool:
    return True
```

Environment:

- Python version: 3.12
- Werkzeug version: 3.1.7 (main branch)

issue_snapshot.title: ThreadCache workers leak the spawning thread's contextvars.Context on free-threaded builds
issue_snapshot.body:
**Environment**
- Python 3.14.2 free-threading build
- trio: 0.33.0
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

On python314t+ free threaded build, `ThreadCache`'s pooled
`WorkerThreads` can retain a strong reference to whatever `contextvars.Context`
was active in the thread that first caused them to be spawned for the life of the pooled thread.

**Repro**
```python
import contextvars
import gc
import sys
import trio

cvar: contextvars.ContextVar[object] = contextvars.ContextVar("cvar")

async def main() -> None:
    class Foo:
        pass

    def sync_fn():
        pass

    contextval = Foo()
    cvar.set(contextval)
    await trio.to_thread.run_sync(sync_fn)
    cvar.set(Foo())  # drop our own reference; nothing legitimate should still hold contextval
    gc.collect()

    referrers = [
        r for r in gc.get_referrers(contextval)
        if type(r).__name__ != "coroutine"  # this frame's own locals; expected
    ]
    gil = sys._is_gil_enabled() if hasattr(sys, "_is_gil_enabled") else "N/A (<3.13)"
    print(f"GIL enabled: {gil}")
    print(f"unexpected referrers: {referrers}")

    assert not referrers, f"leaked referrers after to_thread.run_sync: {referrers}"

trio.run(main)
```
python 314t: 
```
GIL enabled: False
unexpected referrers: [<hamt_bitmap_node object at 0x3f9b2fb2c40>]
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ......
AssertionError: leaked referrers after to_thread.run_sync: [<hamt_bitmap_node object at 0x3f9b2fb2c40>]
```
python 314:
```
GIL enabled: True
unexpected referrers: []
```
**expected**
```
GIL enabled: True
unexpected referrers: []
```
**Related**:
https://github.com/agronholm/anyio/issues/1220

issue_snapshot.title: websockets changed how it handles non-ASCII headers
issue_snapshot.body:
### Initial Checks

- [ ] I confirm this was discussed, and the maintainers suggest I open an issue.
- [x] I'm aware that if I created this issue without a discussion, it may be closed without a response.

_we didn't discuss this, but we collaborated before and I'm sure it's an actual issue_

### Description

In websockets 16.1 and in the upcoming 17.0, I changed how non-ASCII headers, which the HTTP spec disallows, are handled by websockets. This happened over two releases because I messed up and then cleaned up.

This will be backwards-incompatible for uvicorn; your tests will blow up next time you run them; and it has already blown up here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16030 :-(

1. websockets 16.1 changed **receiving non-ASCII headers** from `.decode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape")` to `.decode("latin-1")` which never crashes, is fully reversible, and is what older versions of HTTP more or less tolerated; at least it's less esoteric than surrogate escapes. Currently, you're relying on the (undocumented) decoding algorithm to [undo it by re-encoding](https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn/blob/7e11cc65f0642c823ef18ea01ff6b23af90aaa9e/uvicorn/protocols/websockets/websockets_sansio_impl.py#L196). This needs to be changed to `value.encode("latin-1"))`. Options for fixing:
  a. uvicorn switches to latin-1 to match websockets and requires websockets >=16.1
  b. uvicorn picks ascii + surrogate escapes or latin-1, conditional on the version of websockets — better if you don't want to constrain the version of websockets, but needs cleaning up later
  c. I release a 16.1.1 that undoes this change, and we solve it with a. or b. for websockets 17.0.

2. websockets 17.0 (not released yet) will change **sending non-ASCII headers** from `.encode()` to `.encode("latin-1")`. This ensures clean round-trips, accounting for the first change. Also this makes it possible to send anything that doesn't break HTTP, while previously only valid UTF-8 could be sent. Currently, you have a [test that sends a non-ASCII header](https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn/blob/7e11cc65f0642c823ef18ea01ff6b23af90aaa9e/tests/protocols/test_websocket.py#L214). That will break. Options for fixing:
  a. add a `.encode().decode("latin-1")` somewhere in uvicorn to stick to UTF-8 and require websockets >= 17.0
  b. same as a., but conditional on the version of websockets 
  c. assert that the header is set to `bytes("abraão", "latin-1")` and require websockets >= 17.0; document the backwards incompatibility
  d. same as c., but conditional on the version of websockets 

I'm sorry I underestimated the backwards incompatibility :-(

This affects only the small subset of users how receive non-spec-compliant headers in the first place, so it's not major drama, but still worth fixing.

I'm happy to provide a PR for your favorite options.

### Python, Uvicorn & OS Version

```Text
0.51.0
```

issue_snapshot.title: websockets-sansio: WebSocket Denial Response emits duplicate Content-Type / Content-Length
issue_snapshot.body:
### Summary

On the `websockets-sansio` implementation, a WebSocket Denial Response (`websocket.http.response.*`) is written with uvicorn's own synthesized `Content-Type` and `Content-Length` **plus** the application's headers, rather than the application's alone. The `websockets` and `wsproto` implementations emit the same response correctly.

This matters because `--ws auto` resolves to `WebSocketsSansIOProtocol` whenever `websockets` is installed, so it's the default path for most installs.

### Versions

```
uvicorn    0.51.0
websockets 16.1.1
python     3.12.7
```

### Reproduction

Dependency-free ASGI app that rejects the handshake with a JSON 422:

```python
import base64, os, socket, threading, time
import uvicorn

BODY = b'{"detail":"nope"}'

async def app(scope, receive, send):
    assert scope["type"] == "websocket"
    await receive()  # websocket.connect
    await send({
        "type": "websocket.http.response.start",
        "status": 422,
        "headers": [(b"content-type", b"application/json")],
    })
    await send({"type": "websocket.http.response.body", "body": BODY})

def serve(port, impl):
    cfg = uvicorn.Config(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=port, log_level="critical", ws=impl)
    s = uvicorn.Server(cfg)
    threading.Thread(target=s.run, daemon=True).start()
    while not s.started:
        time.sleep(0.05)
    return s

def handshake(port):
    key = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(16)).decode()
    req = (f"GET /ws HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:{port}\r\n"
           f"Upgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\n"
           f"Sec-WebSocket-Key: {key}\r\nSec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n")
    s = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=5)
    s.sendall(req.encode()); s.settimeout(3)
    chunks = []
    try:
        while True:
            b = s.recv(4096)
            if not b: break
            chunks.append(b)
    except socket.timeout:
        pass
    s.close()
    return b"".join(chunks)

for impl, port in (("websockets", 8811), ("wsproto", 8812), ("websockets-sansio", 8813)):
    srv = serve(port, impl)
    print(f"--- {impl} ---")
    print(handshake(port).split(b"\r\n\r\n")[0].decode())
    print()
    srv.should_exit = True
    time.sleep(0.5)
```

### Actual

```
--- uvicorn --ws websockets ---
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 18:37:09 GMT
Content-Length: 17
Connection: close

--- uvicorn --ws wsproto ---
HTTP/1.1 422
content-type: application/json
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

--- uvicorn --ws websockets-sansio ---
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 18:37:10 GMT
Connection: close
Content-Length: 17
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8      <-- uvicorn's own
content-type: application/json               <-- the application's
```

Note the ordering: a client that takes the first `Content-Type` sees `text/plain; charset=utf-8` for a JSON body.

With a framework response that sets its own `Content-Length` (any Starlette/FastAPI `JSONResponse`, for example), `Content-Length` is duplicated as well:

```
Content-Length: 164
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
content-length: 164
content-type: application/json
```

In that form the `websockets` client rejects the response outright with `InvalidMessage` instead of surfacing the status and body.

### Expected

The application's headers only, as the other two implementations produce.

### Cause

`websockets_sansio_impl.py`, in the `websocket.http.response.body` branch:

```python
response = self.conn.reject(self.initial_response[0], body.decode())
response.headers.update(self.initial_response[1])
```

`conn.reject()` builds a complete response, deriving `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` and `Content-Length` from the body text. `websockets.datastructures.Headers.update()` then **appends** rather than replaces:

```python
>>> h = Headers()
>>> h["Content-Type"] = "text/plain; charset=utf-8"
>>> h.update([("content-type", "application/json")])
>>> list(h.raw_items())
[('Content-Type', 'text/plain; charset=utf-8'), ('content-type', 'application/json')]
```

so both sets reach the wire. `websockets_impl.py` and `wsproto_impl.py` build the response from the application's headers only, which is why they're unaffected.

### Note

I haven't sent a PR because the right fix depends on a preference I don't want to guess at â€” deleting uvicorn's synthesized content headers before `update()`, versus constructing the rejection so they're never generated. Happy to put one together if you'd like to indicate which.

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

```python import ssl from celery import Celery # AWS ElastiCache or any TLS-only Redis endpoint REDIS_URL = "redis://:password@my-redis.cache.amazonaws.com:6379/0" ssl_options = {"ssl_cert_reqs": ssl.CERT_NONE} # This raises ValueError on worker startup: # "SSL connection parameters have been provided but the specified URL scheme # is redis://. A Redis SSL connection URL should use the scheme rediss://." app = Celery( "myapp", broker=REDIS_URL, backend=REDIS_URL, # redis:// here causes the crash broker_use_ssl=ssl_options, redis_backend_use_ssl=ssl_options, ) # Workaround: use different URL schemes for broker and backend REDIS_URL_TLS = "rediss://:password@my-redis.cache.amazonaws.com:6379/0" app = Celery( "myapp", broker=REDIS_URL, # redis:// works with broker_use_ssl via Kombu backend=REDIS_URL_TLS, # rediss:// required by Celery backend broker_use_ssl=ssl_options, redis_backend_use_ssl=ssl_options, ) Expected Behavior Both broker_use_ssl and redis_backend_use_ssl should accept the same URL scheme, or the documentation should clearly state the asymmetry. A user connecting to a TLS-only Redis naturally uses the same URL and SSL config for both broker and backend. The current behavior forces them to use redis:// for the broker and rediss:// for the backend — an inconsistency that is not documented and produces a cryptic CRITICAL/MainProcess Unrecoverable error on worker startup. Alternatively, Kombu's broker transport should also raise (or at least warn) when broker_use_ssl is combined with a redis:// URL scheme, to match the backend's strict validation. Currently Kombu silently accepts it (and it happens to work in 5.6.x), while the backend hard-rejects it. Actual Behavior Worker crashes immediately at startup with: [CRITICAL/MainProcess] Unrecoverable error: ValueError( '\nSSL connection parameters have been provided but the specified URL scheme is redis://. A Redis SSL connection URL should use the scheme rediss://.\n') Traceback (most recent call last): File "celery/worker/worker.py", line 203, in start self.blueprint.start(self) File "celery/apps/worker.py", line 238, in startup_info results=self.app.backend.as_uri(), File "celery/app/base.py", line 1474, in backend self._backend = self._get_backend() File "celery/backends/redis.py", line 279, in __init__ self.connparams = self._params_from_url(url, self.connparams) File "celery/backends/redis.py", line 343, in _params_from_url raise ValueError(E_REDIS_SSL_PARAMS_AND_SCHEME_MISMATCH) ValueError: SSL connection parameters have been provided but the specified URL scheme is redis://. A Redis SSL connection URL should use the scheme rediss://. The same error also surfaces from kafka consumer workers when calling apply_async: File "celery/app/base.py", line 970, in send_task result = (result_cls or self.AsyncResult)(task_id) File "celery/backends/redis.py", line 343, in _params_from_url raise ValueError(E_REDIS_SSL_PARAMS_AND_SCHEME_MISMATCH) Note: broker_use_ssl with redis:// works correctly in Kombu 5.6.2 (TLS connection is established). The inconsistency is exclusively in the backend validation.

issue_snapshot.title: make_aware() silently mishandles spring-forward DST gap — crontab tasks scheduled in a non-existent local time are skipped or run with wrong UTC offset
issue_snapshot.body:
# Checklist - [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `main` branch of Celery. - [x] This has already been asked to the [discussions forum](https://github.com/celery/celery/discussions) first. - [x] I have read the relevant section in the [contribution guide](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/main/contributing.html#other-bugs) on reporting bugs. - [x] I have checked the [issues list](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Issue+Type%3A+Bug+Report%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22) for similar or identical bug reports. - [x] I have checked the [pull requests list](https://github.com/celery/celery/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3A%22PR+Type%3A+Bugfix%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22) for existing proposed fixes. - [x] I have checked the [commit log](https://github.com/celery/celery/commits/main) to find out if the bug was already fixed in the main branch. - [x] I have included all related issues and possible duplicate issues in this issue (If there are none, check this box anyway). - [ ] I have tried to reproduce the issue with [pytest-celery](https://docs.celeryq.dev/projects/pytest-celery/en/latest/userguide/celery-bug-report.html) and added the reproduction script below. ## Mandatory Debugging Information - [ ] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue. - [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `main` branch of Celery. - [ ] I have included the contents of ``pip freeze`` in the issue. - [ ] I have included all the versions of all the external dependencies required to reproduce this bug. ## Optional Debugging Information - [x] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one Python version and/or implementation. - [x] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one operating system. ## Related Issues and Possible Duplicates #### Related Issues - #10107 — Hourly crontab skips execution during **fall-back** DST transition (the complementary issue; that PR introduced `_is_ambiguous` handling but did not address the spring-forward gap) #### Possible Duplicates - None ## Environment & Settings **Celery version**: main (post-5.4) **Relevant config**: ```python CELERY_TIMEZONE = "US/Eastern" # or any DST-observing zone CELERY_ENABLE_UTC = True ``` # Steps to Reproduce ## Required Dependencies - **Minimal Python Version**: 3.9 - **Minimal Celery Version**: 5.3 (after pytz deprecation / ZoneInfo migration) - **Minimal Kombu Version**: N/A - **Minimal Broker Version**: N/A - **Minimal Result Backend Version**: N/A - **Minimal OS and/or Kernel Version**: Any - **Minimal Broker Client Version**: N/A - **Minimal Result Backend Client Version**: N/A ### Python Packages
pip freeze Output:

celery @ git+https://github.com/celery/celery@main python-dateutil>=2.8

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

```python from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo from datetime import datetime from dateutil import tz as dateutil_tz from celery.utils.time import make_aware tz = ZoneInfo("US/Eastern") # March 10, 2024: clocks spring forward at 2:00 AM -> 3:00 AM # 2:30 AM does not exist in US/Eastern on this date non_existent_dt = datetime(2024, 3, 10, 2, 30, 0) # Confirm it truly doesn't exist assert not dateutil_tz.datetime_exists(non_existent_dt.replace(tzinfo=tz)), \ "Expected non-existent time in spring-forward gap" result = make_aware(non_existent_dt, tz) # The UTC offset will be -05:00 (EST) instead of the correct post-transition -04:00 (EDT) # The function returns silently with no warning or error print(result) print(result.utcoffset()) # prints -1 day, 19:00:00 (i.e. -05:00, which is wrong) # To see the beat scheduler impact: from celery.schedules import crontab schedule = crontab(hour=2, minute=30, app=None) # On the spring-forward night, remaining_delta produces a next-run datetime # landing in the gap, which make_aware() resolves incorrectly, # causing the task to either be skipped or fire an hour late. ```

# Expected Behavior `make_aware()` should detect when a naive datetime falls inside a spring-forward DST gap (a time that does not exist in the given timezone) and advance the datetime to the first valid moment after the gap — consistent with how most DST-aware frameworks (Django, Arrow, pendulum) handle this case. `dateutil_tz.datetime_exists()` is already available via the existing `from dateutil import tz as dateutil_tz` import in `celery/utils/time.py` and can be used directly. Proposed fix in `celery/utils/time.py`: ```python def make_aware(dt: datetime, tz: tzinfo) -> datetime: """Set timezone for a :class:`~datetime.datetime` object.""" dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=tz) if _is_ambiguous(dt, tz): # Fall-back: two wall-clock instants map to the same local time. # Pick the earlier UTC instant (fold=0, DST still active). dt = min(dt.replace(fold=0), dt.replace(fold=1)) elif _can_detect_ambiguous(tz) and not dateutil_tz.datetime_exists(dt): # Spring-forward gap: this local time does not exist. # Advance to the post-transition instant (fold=1). dt = dt.replace(fold=1) return dt ``` A corresponding `_is_nonexistent()` helper (mirroring `_is_ambiguous()`) could also be added for clarity and testability. # Actual Behavior `make_aware()` only guards against ambiguous (fall-back) times via `_is_ambiguous()`. There is no equivalent check for non-existent (spring-forward) times. When a crontab's computed next-run datetime lands inside the spring-forward gap: 1. `make_aware()` calls `dt.replace(tzinfo=tz)` on the non-existent time with no further correction. 2. The resulting datetime carries the pre-transition UTC offset (e.g. `-05:00` EST instead of `-04:00` EDT). 3. `remaining_estimate()` therefore computes a next-run time that is **one hour later than intended** in UTC. 4. On the affected night the task either **fires one hour late** or is **silently skipped** entirely, with no log warning or exception raised. This is the exact spring-forward counterpart to #10107 (fall-back skipping), but currently has no handling in the codebase. I WOULD LIKE TO WORK ON THIS ISSUE AND GET IT FIXED AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. PLEASE ASSIGN IT TO ME.

issue_snapshot.title: Inconsistent number of lines after import
issue_snapshot.body:
**Describe the bug**

If the first thing after the import is a class, optionally with an arbitrary comment - black makes the separation as 2 lines - in line with PEP-8.
Unless the comment is `# fmt: off` - then black ignores that there's a class, and makes it one empty line, conflicting with various other hooks in our pre-commit.

**To Reproduce**

```python
import sys


# fmt: off
class C:
    def foo(self):
        print(sys.platform)
```

**Expected behavior**

Always 2 lines in this case. 

**Environment**

- Black's version: 26.5.1
- OS and Python version: Windows 11/Python 3.12.10

**Additional context**

* Both flake8 and isort insist on 2 lines here.
* While flake8 can be pacified, isort can't be and cannot reproduce this behavior with any settings.
* PEP-8 says 2 lines.
* We usually toggle black off for the test classes to make them readable.

issue_snapshot.title: Magic trailing comma does not explode a type-parameter list containing *TypeVarTuple / **ParamSpec
issue_snapshot.body:
**Describe the bug**

A [magic trailing comma](https://black.readthedocs.io/en/stable/the_black_code_style/current_style.html#the-magic-trailing-comma) correctly explodes a PEP 695 type-parameter list of plain type vars (one per line), but is **silently ignored once the list contains a `*TypeVarTuple` or `**ParamSpec`** — the params collapse back onto a single line.

**To Reproduce**

```python
class C[
    T,
    *Ts,
    **P,
]:
    pass
```

Running `black --target-version py312` (stable style) produces:

```python
class C[
    T, *Ts, **P,
]:
    pass
```

The same construct with only plain type vars is exploded as expected:

```python
class C[
    T,
    U,
    V,
]:
    pass
```

It reproduces on `def`/`async def`/`type` aliases too, and regardless of `--target-version` (autodetected). In a `def`, the argument list still explodes correctly while the type-param list collapses, e.g. `def f[T, *Ts, **P,](x):` -> the `[...]` collapses but `(x,)` explodes.

**Expected behavior**

The magic trailing comma should force the type-parameter list to explode one-per-line, identical to the plain-type-var case, whether or not the list contains a `*TypeVarTuple`/`**ParamSpec`.

**Environment**

- Black's version: 26.5.2.dev29+gb74b23013 (commit b74b230), also reproduces on current `main`
- OS and Python version: Linux, CPython 3.14

**Additional context**

The collapsed output is stable and AST-equivalent, so it does not trip idempotency/AST-safety checks — it's purely a splitting-decision bug specific to starred type params.
issue_snapshot.author: Emilianocarfu88

issue_snapshot.title: `IncompleteRead` exception crashes pip instantly, bypassing the built-in download resumption logic
issue_snapshot.body: ### Description When `pip download` encounters a sudden network disruption mid-transfer, the underlying network layer throws a protocol exception, such as `http.client.IncompleteRead`. Because this exception is not gracefully intercepted during the stream-reading phase, it instantly crashes the entire application execution context. As a result, `pip` immediately aborts the operation, completely bypassing its own downstream self-healing mechanisms (`_attempt_resumes_or_redownloads` / `_http_get_resume`) which were explicitly designed to issue HTTP Range requests and resume incomplete transfers. ### Expected behavior `pip` should recognize the stream-reading failure as a recoverable network event. Instead of crashing, it should transition the current download state safely into the resumption flow, allowing the client to utilize standard HTTP `206 Partial Content` handshakes to patch and complete the missing chunks seamlessly. ### pip version 26.1.1 ### Python version 3.13 ### OS Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS ### How to Reproduce 1. Save the following script as `server.py` and run it locally. This mock registry serves a 100MB fake package but intentionally cuts the connection via a hard TCP `RST` signal exactly after delivering 10MB to trigger an `IncompleteRead` on the client side: ```python import os import socket import re from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer # Definitive test asset (Simulating a 100MB heavy wheel) FAKE_FILE_SIZE = 100 * 1024 * 1024 WHEEL_FILENAME = "test_package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl" # Global session/connection tracker connection_count = 0 class HellMockRegistryHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_GET(self): global connection_count # 1. Standard PEP-503 Simple Repository API routing if self.path in ["/simple/test-package/", "/simple/test-package"]: self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8") self.end_headers() html = f'{WHEEL_FILENAME}' self.wfile.write(html.encode('utf-8')) return # 2. Heavy wheel payload stream distribution routing if self.path == f"/packages/{WHEEL_FILENAME}": connection_count += 1 range_header = self.headers.get("Range") print(f"\n⚡ [Session #{connection_count}] Inbound request captured!") start_byte = 0 # Inspecting HTTP Range headers for chunk resumption validations if range_header: match = re.match(r"bytes=(\d+)-", range_header) if match: start_byte = int(match.group(1)) print(f" 🎯 [RESUME BRANCH] Pip requesting offset from {start_byte // (1024*1024)}MB.") self.send_response(206) self.send_header("Content-Range", f"bytes {start_byte}-{FAKE_FILE_SIZE-1}/{FAKE_FILE_SIZE}") else: print(f" 🆕 [FRESH BRANCH] Pip initiating cold download from 0MB.") self.send_response(200) # Providing matching tokens to trick pip's conditional headers validation self.send_header("ETag", '"hell-mock-999"') self.send_header("Last-Modified", "Wed, 18 Jun 2026 00:00:00 GMT") remaining_bytes = FAKE_FILE_SIZE - start_byte self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream") self.send_header("Content-Length", str(remaining_bytes)) self.end_headers() # ---------------------------------------------------- # MALICIOUS SLICING: Enforce connection drop after 10MB # ---------------------------------------------------- MAX_TRANSMIT = 10 * 1024 * 1024 # 10MB threshold limit chunk_size = 64 * 1024 bytes_sent_this_session = 0 try: while bytes_sent_this_session < remaining_bytes: self.wfile.write(b"\x00" * min(chunk_size, remaining_bytes - bytes_sent_this_session)) bytes_sent_this_session += chunk_size # Connection severance trigger if bytes_sent_this_session >= MAX_TRANSMIT: current_total = start_byte + bytes_sent_this_session print(f" 💥 [SOCKET KILL] Pushed {bytes_sent_this_session // (1024*1024)}MB this session. (Global Progress: {current_total // (1024*1024)}MB/100MB). Force-closing stream via RST...") # Set SO_LINGER to 0 to send a hard TCP RST packet back to client self.request.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, b'\x01\x00\x00\x00') self.request.close() return print(" 🎉 [SUCCESS] Final data boundary reached. Stream completed.") except Exception as e: print(f" [EXCEPTION] Stream transfer interrupted: {e}") return self.send_error(404, "Not Found") if __name__ == '__main__': print("==================================================") print(" Mock Pip Server (Hell Mode) active on port 8080") print("==================================================") HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 8080), HellMockRegistryHandler).serve_forever() ``` 2. ### Description

When running poetry publish in a CI environment with the --no-interaction flag, Poetry still prompts for confirmation if build artifacts already exist in the dist/ directory.

Example prompt:

There are 2 files ready for publishing. Build anyway? (yes/no) [no]

This works fine when running locally, but in CI/CD environments (for example Bitbucket Pipelines or GitHub Actions) there is no interactive input available. As a result, the pipeline stops waiting for input and eventually fails.

issue_snapshot.title: Poetry thinks Conda env is active after it's been deactivated
issue_snapshot.body:
### Description

I am using Anaconda with the `auto_activate_base` option disabled (i.e., `conda config --set auto_activate_base false`), so that Conda is only active when I've explicitly activated it. After activating and then deactivating a Conda environment, this leads to an edge case that causes incorrect behavior in the `poetry env use` command:

* Before activating the environment:
    * System Python is first in the path.
    * The CONDA_PREFIX variable is unset.
    * Poetry correctly assumes that a virtualenv is not active, and creates a local venv.
* After running `conda activate $HOME/envs/foo`:
    * $HOME/envs/foo is first in the path.
    * CONDA_PREFIX is set to $HOME/envs/foo.
    * Poetry correctly assumes that $HOME/envs/foo is active and uses it.
* After running `conda deactivate`:
    * System Python takes precedence in PATH.
    * **CONDA_PREFIX is set, but its value is an empty string (!).**
    * Because CONDA_PREFIX is set (but empty), Poetry thinks a venv is active.
    * `poetry env use` tries to run `python` with an empty prefix, but cannot find `python` in the path and fails.

The problem is due to https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/blob/0e02be7c1a1aa132035b109e1fe0800676a4d83a/src/poetry/utils/env/env_manager.py#L217 To confirm that a virtualenv is active, it should check that env_prefix is neither None **nor an empty string**.

### Workarounds

Manually run `unset CONDA_PREFIX` after `conda deactivate`.

### Poetry Installation Method

other

### Operating System

Ubuntu 20.04.3

### Poetry Version

Poetry (version 2.3.2)

### Poetry Configuration

```bash session
(note: `$USER` in the below is not literal, but redacts my actual username from the server)


cache-dir = "/home/$USER/.cache/pypoetry"
data-dir = "/home/$USER/.local/share/pypoetry"
installer.max-workers = null

requests.max-retries = 0
solver.lazy-wheel = true

issue_snapshot.title: BaseSettings.update() does not accept iterable key-value pairs
issue_snapshot.body:
`BaseSettings` inherits from `MutableMapping`, but `BaseSettings.update()` does not accept iterable key-value pairs like `dict.update()` does.

### Example:

```python
from scrapy.settings import BaseSettings

settings = BaseSettings({"KEY": 0})
settings.update([("KEY", 1)])
```

### This raises:

```text
AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'items'
```

There is already an xfailed test for this in `tests/test_settings/__init__.py::TestBaseSettings::test_update_iterable`.

issue_snapshot.title: get_func_args_dict doesn't support PEP649 lazy annotation loading
issue_snapshot.body:
### Description
Hi scrapy team, in 3.14 `inspect.signature()` on type-annotated functions isn't safe at runtime as types are lazy in 3.14.

### Steps to Reproduce

```py
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import scrapy


class SomeMiddleware:
    def process_exception(self, request: scrapy.Request, exception: Exception) -> None:
        pass

from scrapy.utils.python import get_func_args_dict

get_func_args_dict(SomeMiddleware().process_exception)  # crashes here
```

**Expected behavior:** 
`get_func_args_dict` returns (dict of arguments)

**Actual behavior:** 
Raises NameError: name 'scrapy' is not defined instead of returning. 

**Reproduces how often:** 
N/A / Always with Python 3.14

### Versions
```
Scrapy       : 2.17.0
lxml         : 6.1.1
libxml2      : 2.14.6
cssselect    : 1.5.0
parsel       : 1.11.0

### Additional context
Found this when using `ruff`'s TC rules ([TC002](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/typing-only-third-party-import/)).
